runs.text: The documents do not say that cobalt-free cathodes in general have flat voltage profiles. The only explicit statement about voltage-profile shape for a cobalt-free class is the opposite: the review lists sloping profiles as a drawback of disordered-rocksalt (DRX) cathodes. Among the challenges for DRX cathodes it names:
from the extent of transition-metal cation disorder. The review frames DRX as a low-Co/Co-free system it discusses alongside others:

support.quote: including layered, spinel, olivine, and DRX systems

runs.text: . For the other cobalt-free families (Mn-substituted LNO, NFA, and NM82, NMT, NMM and NMA), their charge/discharge profiles appear in the figures, but the text does not describe their shape as flat or sloping, so the documents give no answer for them.
